title: Mathematicians challenge AI with 50 of mathematics' hardest open problems
key_facts: Epoch AI's FrontierMath: Open Problems expanded in July to 50 research problems chosen by mathematicians.
Problems were proposed at June workshops in London, Toronto, Los Angeles, New York, Berkeley and Boston.
Each problem comes with a computer verifier that can check a proposed answer.
By 31 July Epoch said three of the 50 had been solved by AI.
Examples: Sum of Three Cubes (n=114 open), an Apery-style irrationality proof for zeta(5), the Lonely Runner Conjecture.
In September researchers reported a general solution to the core problem in approval-based committee elections, with a proof obtained with GPT-6 Astra and checked in Lean.
quote_evidence: Epoch AI says the problems have resisted serious human attempts and that a solution should represent meaningful progress in mathematical knowledge.
By July 31, Epoch said three of the 50 problems had already been solved by AI.
In September, researchers also reported a general solution to the 'core' problem in approval-based committee elections, with a proof obtained with GPT-6 Astra and checked in Lean.
why_it_matters_hint: A computer-checked set of real open problems makes AI math claims easier to test.
event_date: List expanded July 2026; status as of 31 Jul 2026; September result
notes: Feature published 4 Oct 2026 about a July list; lowered 6 to 5 as not new today.
